seo.metaDescription: Moving from 0.9 to 1.0: the breaking changes with the code before and after, and what is new.

props.markdown: This page lists what changes when you move from 0.9 to 1.0. Each breaking change shows the 0.9 code, then a live example of the 1.0 code. The additive changes need no action. For what 1.x keeps stable, see [Stability](/docs/stability).
Four changes can break a build or change what a chart draws. Go through them in order.

In the library, solid is an actual value and hatch is a plan or a reference. A bare `<RankedBars>` now draws solid bars; in 0.9 it drew hatched ones. RankedBars: pass `fill="hatch"` to keep the old look.

props.text: A chart needs a title or aria-labelledby

props.markdown: `Chart` and the 11 high-level charts now require an accessible name in their types: a `title`, or an `aria-labelledby` that points at an element naming the chart. A chart with neither is a type error. The development warning stays for calls from JavaScript. With both props, `aria-labelledby` names the chart and `title` stays the default caption of the data table.
After, with a heading that already names the chart. `aria-labelledby` points at the id of the heading:

`ChartProps` and every `*Props` of the 11 charts are now type aliases, an intersection with the new exported type `ChartName`, not interfaces. So `interface … extends BarChartProps<D>` no longer compiles. Use `type … = BarChartProps<D> & {…}`:

Do not wrap a props type in `Pick` or `Omit`. They collapse the union of `ChartName` and the chart loses the requirement of a name. If you must, add it back with `& ChartName`: `type MyProps<D> = Omit<BarChartProps<D>, 'height'> & ChartName`.

props.text: An invalid date breaks the line

props.markdown: `Area` and `LineChart` no longer join the line, band or area across a date that isn’t a date, or across a missing value. They break there, as `Line` and `Band` already did: a series with a bad date in the middle draws two segments instead of one. To keep the old joined line, filter the rows before you pass them. The same filter keeps an `Area` joined; for a missing value, filter out the rows whose value is `null` or `NaN`.

The wording of the strings the library writes itself, such as the keyboard hint, is not part of the public API and can change in a minor release (see [Stability](/docs/stability)). Pass your own `keyboardHint`, or another text you control, wherever you need to know the exact words. In tests, don’t search by the built-in text: find the chart by its `title` and role.

props.code: expect(screen.getByText('Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.')).toBeInTheDocument()

props.markdown: After: a `keyboardHint` you pass is used as is, so you can assert on it.
These need no action. They are new in 1.0.
`LineChart` takes an `underlay`: an element drawn after the grid and before the lines, for example an `Area` with last year’s values. See [LineChart](/docs/line-chart) for the props.

`createDateFormatter(spec, options)` builds a function from epoch milliseconds to a string, in `'day'`, `'month'`, `'quarter'`, `'year'`, `'auto'` or any `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions`. It is exported from `tally-charts/core` with three types: `DateFormatSpec` for the first argument, `DateFormatOptions` for the second and `DateFormatter` for the result. See [Formatting](/docs/formatting).

props.text: The Enter hint only on selectable points

props.markdown: The keyboard hint adds “Press Enter to select.” only while the active point can be selected: the chart has `onSelect` and the point doesn’t have `selectable: false`. In 0.9 the sentence could promise Enter on a chart where it did nothing. Tab into the chart below and listen; remove `onSelect` and the sentence is gone.
